{{Quote|I didn't think you saw it.''"<br />"''It was a ''giant tower'', of course I saw it.|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker, on the Son's tower|<ref name="Altar of Mortis (episode)">{{TCW|Altar of Mortis (episode)}}</ref>}}
The '''Son's cathedral''' was the residence of the [[Son/Legends|Son]] located in the region of [[Mortis/Legends|Mortis]] where the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] was strongest.

==Structure==
[[File:SonsTower2-AOM.png|thumb|left|180px|The primary central tower]]
The primary structure of the cathedral was a high tower supporting a huge sphere, full of a strange substance that luminously glowed green. Circling the base of the tower were four smaller towers with green spheres atop each of them connected by a wall. Inside the tower, there was a large circular window that overlooked a large courtyard. Beneath the window was the Son's throne chamber. The inside had a high ceiling, more than twice as high as the total height of the Son in his [[Gargoyle/Legends|gargoyle form]]. Inside, there was also a prison, in which the Son would hold [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] prisoner.

==History==
Around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], the Son had kidnapped [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] and locked her up there. He then poisoned her, causing her to become a Dark-sider and he watched as she attacked [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] when they had come to rescue her. At the same time, he was confronted by [[Daughter/Legends|Daughter]] and later [[Father (Mortis)/Legends|Father]] and the tower became a battleground for both the Jedi and the powerful Force-users. The result ended with Daughter dying after sacrificing herself to save Father, Son escaping and Ahsoka recovering back to normal.

==Behind the scenes==
The Son's cathedral first appeared in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series episode "[[Altar of Mortis (episode)|Altar of Mortis]]."

The tower was based on the tower of [[Wikipedia:Isengard#Orthanc|Orthanc]] from [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings|''Lord of the Rings'']] [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings film trilogy|films]] and was made to resemble the staff of the evil wizard [[Wikipedia:Saruman|Saruman the White]]. The location's concept also drew inspiration from [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s sketches of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]] (before the location was changed to the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]).<ref name="SWArchive-''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Altar of Mortis">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode316.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Altar of Mortis}}</ref>
